To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the main reasons for the emergence and existence for the NGOs are: (i) to provide public goods, (ii) to provide private goods, (iii) to provide public services, (iv) to provide private services, (v) to provide tax subsidies, (vi) to reduce the cost of production, (vii) to reduce the risk of production, (vi) and to provide a forum to the stakeholders.
NGOs are a vital part of our society.
the NGOs have appeared and emerged in the society due to the reasons of public goods, tax subsidy and contract failure and they are working for the betterment of the society and the country.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical analysis of the reasons of emergence and existence of NGO in Bangladesh.
the theories that govern the NGO operations.
the theories of NGOs and their applications in the Bangladesh context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NGOs are not a substitute of the government but a complement to the state in the development process of a country.
NGOs are the most effective tools of the socio economic development in the society.
the NGOs are the most important and vital part of the society.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NGOs are not only the alternative to the government but also a complementary to it.
the NGOs are the best means of social and economic development in the society.
, NGOs in Bangladesh should be considered as a part of the civil society, which is the third force in Bangladesh after the government and the private sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Stakeholder theory has a great potential to be applied in the Banglaeshi NGO context.
NGOs are not only the providers of public goods, but also they are the providers of private goods, which are not provided by the market and the state, and are not provided by any other organization.
NGOs can be a powerful tool to fight poverty in Bangladesh.
